reviews.title: Bad App - Pure Bait and switch tactics
reviews.text:
Boo is flooded with fake profiles, bots and scammers whilst the developers are also scamming the users themselves.

The app sends waves of fake profiles to like your profile to trick you into buying a subscription. As soon as you pay, your profile goes quiet until your subscription ends with zero interaction.

On top of that, the location filters do not work at all.

Even if you block specific regions, you will still get bombarded with likes from international profiles using false travel locations to get around the filters (mainly from Indonesia and Africa) that are either scams or fakes. Save your money and time.

Compared to other apps, this is the one of the most disgusting scams of an application out of them all.

reviews.title: Some places are good, but unfortunately, it seems the ball is dropped in others
reviews.text:
The app Work good for making friends. The feature of having interest and posting on the board is pretty cool, but where it falls flat. Dating often with these apps you’ll have your limited amount of interactions in this one even your not interested swipes count so when it comes to people liking you, it seems to be days if not weeks before you’re able to like them back unless of course you pay money for a weekly pass. My biggest interest was it making a point Of being anti-ghosting but unfortunately, from the time I’ve used it I know that’s a load at this point swiping does not mean anything, especially in the case of you can go and fill out your entire profile get a single view in a span of a week, but somebody who has a single picture no interest no bio and is undecided in what they’re seeking is thrown into the spotlight somehow.

That being said use the app as a social media post board since the dating portion seems to be ineffective, even with all the extra shiny bits attached, you will still be encountering many who don’t even have the same interest what they’re seeking and will respond a single time then ghost.

Update after using it longer I can safely say just stick to insta facebook or whatever this app seems to be populated by a sad amount of bots both in the reviews and “users”

reviews.title: The Worst Dating App In Years
reviews.text:
Alright, the onboarding is fun and unique. The app essentially gets you to take a couple different personality tests and helps build your profile for you with that info- cool and new! The issue is after you sign up. You basically get 12 free actions per day - and this is sending likes OR dislikes! Mind you, this app isn’t even trying to sell you from the start by showing you attractive and most interesting people, it’s genuinely some of the most mediocre people I’ve seen across any of the dating apps I’m on - as in constant 2/10s lol. The issue with that though is I can’t even get to attractive & interesting people to like anyone because I literally have to use all my free actions to dislike all the people I’m not interested in. I’ve only been able to like ONE 6/10 person I’m not even interested in within the first 3 days of having this app. Such a shame for what efforts I put into the app for signup. Give me a full app experience with at least one match first before asking me to pay for your stupid coins or subscription. I’m sure
I’m wrong in saying nobody will do that, but I certainly won’t be doing that, and the app is being deleted. It’s a waste of time and space on my phone.

reviews.title: Bit of a waste
reviews.text: I say this as someone who has used this app several times before with moderate success at finding friends but whatever changes and evergreen annoyances add up to an unworthy use of time now. Like most apps nowadays, you have to pay for seamless interaction with others, and paying for premium doesn’t change this if you’re liking someone’s profile that isn’t premium. I gave the 3 month plan a chance and the experience wasn’t nearly improved enough to make it an engaging time killer. The community itself seems very passive, almost dead eyed. Then again, those mundane pleasantries might not be getting typed out by flesh and blood. Relatedly, AI profiles seem to be on the rise. I had the same set of generically Asian woman generated slop show up in my requests five times with different names within the span of two weeks.  The gatekeepers are comatose. I want to like this app and I feel like it did some stuff well, establishing some connections I still foster to this day. Less of a cute Boo, more of a tragic BooHoo in 2026.

reviews.title: The UI is too busy
reviews.text: The app has some great concepts that I’ve wished in the past that other apps I’ve used before app. A lot of thought clearly has been put into it to ensure people get a good experience. However, the UI is so ridiculously overcrowded with all sorts of buttons, tags imagery, text, etc that it can get a bit overwhelming and is actually off-putting. The performance is also pretty sluggish, the app doesn’t feel very optimised. Very aggressive monetisation, for every action it seels like I’m being pushed to subscribe even before I made my mind up about using the app and there are constant pop ups and notifications trying to get me to subscribe.

reviews.title: Frustrating
reviews.text:
I’ve actually met some really cool people on Boo, so the app clearly has potential for forming genuine connections. Unfortunately, the technical issues have ruined almost all of those interactions for me. Messages regularly fail to send, the app freezes constantly, and profiles/conversations seem to disappear randomly.

The result is a lot of unintentional ghosting and broken conversation flow, which is incredibly frustrating when you’re genuinely trying to build lasting connections with people. It creates misunderstandings that make it seem like people are ignoring each other when really the app just isn’t functioning reliably.

I want to like Boo because the people on it have been great but the bugs seriously get in the way of the whole experience.

reviews.title: Not great
reviews.text:
The shining star of this app is the Meyers Briggs comparison and data. Seeing how you’re wired a potential matches are wired, then a compatibility summary is helpful. The social aspect of this app has little to do with actually finding a connection and more to do with expressing yourself. It’s a unique feature but I’m here for dating, not another media warp hole. 
The weakest aspect is the dating pool, it’s small, like really small. Within less than 100 swipes I was already being shown profiles outside of my filtered area. In less than 2 days I had swiped through all the available profiles. When it would “send new souls” I got excited . . . It was literally one each time. One new person a day. Early on I paid for premium to see what it was all about. The coolest feature here is that you can see who has viewed your profile in the last week, not just likes. The major downfall here is that in 7 days it was only showing me the same 10-12 views. You mean I paid for premium , stay actively engaged in the daily questions, and I’ve only been shown to 12 other users. 
What a rip off.

Have met some friends to message, but the dating side of this app is totally worthless right now.

reviews.title: No matches yet and not much of a selection in my area
reviews.text: So I’ve been trying out this app for a little while now it’s kind of disappointing. There’s not many people in my area that are coming up in my potential matches. This site does seem to have less obvious, fake profiles, than the other apps. This app also counts your left swipes in your daily allowance. It would be beneficial if the site only counted your right swipes, and what they allow each day, because the user should not be penalized for being honest and their swipes. I’m fully understand that most women in my part of California are only looking for fun without commitment, so I guess it’s not the fault for having such shallow people, but there seems to be just too many non-commitment minded women on here. I’m one of the last men on earth, looking for an actual, long-term committed relationship with one person, as it should be, which makes it very difficult finding that special person. All in all the sex not too bad, but again, it can allow more daily swiping for us with a free account.

reviews.title: Weird app and alike to a lot of others
reviews.text: I came across this one as I thought it was actually free to join, and all the claims to be “different from other dating apps” was why I signed up. After being on it less than two minutes.. I could see that this is also a greedy & money based app for trying to date or find love? Not sure really why so many apps want to try and take money off us to talk and get to know anyone who’s looking the same values or even date and see where things go.. but I’m not going to. I’ve left this negative review because I find it really off putting to even stick with it - when you are charging people £6 a week to put up with perhaps perverts or creeps who pester? I get this on other dating apps, without the charges. And I have to say also, I wouldn’t pay for a dating app ever because most of them do not work. You need to promote free experiences and if people wish to maybe purchase a dating “add-on” for help / more advice, mental health coaches or maybe classes that we can join to make our dating experiences BETTER?? This is not ideal to ask us to pay to view ugly men, creepy men, perverts etc we do not want to maybe match with! And this is where you’ve gone wrong. I see more negative reviews than positive and can see a lot of people commenting the same

reviews.title: Pointless with basic features behind paywall
reviews.text:
Boo looks great on the surface. Different and fresh from other dating apps. I was excited to get my first like, only to find out that even a basic features such as seeing who liked you is locked behind a paywall with the dating mafia ready to shake you down for money before you can see. 

This concept is so backwards to me. A dating app that doesn't want you to be successful at dating. A dating app that doesn't let you do basic things and encourage you to pay for more features. If you let me do the basics, I will gladly pay for more. If you don't let me do the basics, then that only turns me off from your app, I'll uninstall it, and never give you a cent. I don't know why these dating apps don't understand this. Do you want my money or not? 😅 Because treating us like you're not as serious about dating as we are isn't the way to get money out of people. If you support our journey, we will support yours. It's that simple. Locking seeing likes behind a paywall isn't supporting our journey, so we have no reason or encouragement to support yours. Peace out! ✌️

reviews.title: If it’s too good to be true, it probably is.
reviews.text:
I was suspicious at the amount of likes I got once I barely finished setting up my profile, and upon checking the other reviews I find that the app is populated by bots and girls from South Asia who apparently pretend they are from the uk. 

I strongly recommend that the devs clean out the bots from their user base, and additionally not limit the number of swipes you can do behind a paywall. I had my hopes up with the fancy effects and the introduction graphics saying that this app is for nerds who want to bond over their mutual interests, and something about how the app would encourage profile prestige by games or activities instead of relying on premium options, but lo and behold, just like all the other dating apps, paywalls to see the bots who swarmed you with likes or who viewed you. 

Any new users reading this, think twice and think thrice before considering giving money to any dating app. It’s likely a scam used to fleece lovesick singletons so they can get led on by bots. I’ve not paid because thankfully I’m not desperate and have had plenty of poor experiences with prior dating apps that promised they would be different. Hinge, Tinder, Christian Dating- all the same! 

I’m going to continue to try and meet people in person. Dating apps are a scam and I deserve better than to shell out my hard earned cash just to do what you can already do on social media or in person.

reviews.title: Turned Greedy
reviews.text:
When this app was first released it was a great idea and allowed free users to use normal social connection and messaging options with matches. The developers were also easy to communicate with in the beginning to address concerns about constant soliciting from OF Female profiles and scammer issues. At some point they stopped communicating with their users and made it cumbersome and a pain to try and get in touch with them by making you go through some process just to leave a message via their email. The app is now crawling with ⚠️(Ai GENERATED)⚠️ profiles and strongly believe they hide free users profiles from access of even normal free user communication in app. I used to like this app reguardless of the reoccurring login issues, endless fake profiles, relentless female users trying to funnel you to their off site undignified content or complete app crashes. But it seem as though the developers of this app have just turned a good concept into another greedy cash grab to sustain any benefits you can really get from the app anymore. Not worth the download anymore.
